places.name: Down Ampney, Gloucestershire
places.what: Born in the vicarage, the third child of the vicar Arthur Vaughan Williams and Margaret, née Wedgwood. His father died here on 9 February 1875. The coordinates are those of the village, and do not mark the vicarage itself.

places.name: Leith Hill Place, Holmbury St Mary, Surrey
places.what: After his father’s death in early 1875 his mother took the children to the Wedgwood family house. He gave it to the National Trust in 1945. Coordinates mark Holmbury St Mary, not the house.

places.name: Charterhouse School, Godalming
places.what: Boarded here from January 1887 until July 1890. He organised concerts and felt he had the makings of a fine viola player.

places.name: Royal College of Music, South Kensington, London
places.what: Entered the college in September 1890 and, after two terms, became a pupil of Hubert Parry. He returned in 1895, became a close friend of Gustav Holst and went to Stanford for lessons; after the war he taught composition here.

places.name: Trinity College, Cambridge
places.what: Read history and music, with weekly lessons in London from Parry and teaching from Charles Wood; B.Mus. 1894, history degree 1895.

places.name: South Lambeth, London
places.what: Organist of St Barnabas, a post he disliked and resigned in 1899. The coordinates mark Lambeth, not the church.

places.name: Berlin
places.what: A brief period of study with Max Bruch, after which he returned to his post at St Barnabas. The Society’s biography places it between his marriage in October 1897 and his return to Lambeth, but gives no month.

places.name: Ingrave, Essex
places.what: Took down Bushes and Briars here in December 1903, the first song he collected. Over the next ten years he collected more than 800 songs and carols. Coordinates mark the village.

places.name: Dorking, Surrey (Leith Hill Musical Festival)
places.what: Conducted the first combined concert of the Leith Hill Musical Festival at the Public Hall on 10 May 1905 and remained festival conductor until 1953, rehearsing village choirs and conducting Bach’s St Matthew Passion. Coordinates mark Dorking.

places.name: 13 Cheyne Walk, Chelsea, London
places.what: Moved in November 1905 and lived here for 24 years. The plaque beside his bust in Chelsea Embankment Gardens lists the Sea, London and Pastoral Symphonies, The Lark Ascending, the Tallis Fantasia and Sancta Civitas from these years. The house no longer stands; coordinates mark Cheyne Walk.

places.what: Went out with the 2/4th London Field Ambulance on 22 June 1916 and drove the ambulance wagon up the line at night. The Pastoral Symphony grew from these nights. Coordinates mark the village.

places.what: Settled here in 1929 after living at Holmbury St Mary and St Paul’s Road; Adeline died here in 1951. The Society lists Symphonies 4–7, Serenade to Music, The Pilgrim’s Progress and Hodie among the works composed here. The house was demolished in 1964; the coordinates mark Dorking.
